userStories.title: Define the atomic chat ask file protocol
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the shared schema-v1 file protocol connecting detached children and their launching chat.

**Motivation** — `nax chat` launches `nax run`, `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix` as detached jobs.

**Approach** — One mechanism, two sides, joined by a directory of small JSON files per job.

All files live in one directory per job: `<outputDir>/chat-jobs/<jobId>.asks/` (helper `jobAsksDir(outputDir, jobId)` in `job-store.ts`). Every write is atomic (write a sibling temp file, then rename). `key` = the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the request id (`chatAskKey`), so any request id is a safe file name.

| File | Writer | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `heartbeat.json` | parent | `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "at": "<ISO time>" }` |
| `<key>.ask.json` | child | `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "key", "request": <InteractionRequest>, "askedAt" }` |
| `<key>.answer.json` | parent | `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "requestId", "action", "value"?, "respondedBy": "chat-user" \| "chat-agent", "reason"?, "respondedAt" }` |
| `<key>.settled.json` | child | `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "requestId", "by", "action", "value"?, "settledAt" }` |
| `<key>.notice.json` | child | `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "key", "request": <InteractionRequest>, "at" }` |

`by` in a settled record is the winning response's `respondedBy` (`chat-user`, `chat-agent`, the fallback plugin's value such as `telegram`), or `"timeout"`, or `"cancelled"`.

Answer encoding by request type (the same `InteractionResponse` vocabulary the chain already uses): `confirm` → `action` `"approve"` or `"reject"`; `choose` (including tool approvals) → `action` `"choose"`, `value` = the option key; `input` → `action` `"input"`, `value` = the text.

Constants: `CHAT_ASK_POLL_MS = 500` (child poll), `RUN_ASK_POLL_MS = 1_000` (parent tick, which also rewrites heartbeats), `CHAT_ASK_STALE_MS = 15_000` (a heartbeat older than this, or none, means the chat is closed), `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AGENT_ASKS = 3`. The agent-streak constant is owned by US-012. Define `CHAT_ASKS_FLAG` as `"--chat-asks"`. Use `_chatAskFileDeps` for file system effects. Export protocol helpers/types/constants from `src/interaction/index.ts`. Missing/malformed/unknown-action answers read as undefined; valid neighboring ask records survive malformed JSON. Notices are consumed once; freshness includes exactly the stale boundary.

**Scope** — In: new `src/interaction/chat-ask-files.ts`, barrel exports and temp-directory tests in `test/unit/interaction/chat-ask-files.test.ts`. Out: plugin state machine (US-002..004), directory launch helper (US-008), routing streak (US-012).

**Interface** — Preserve these helper call contracts from the spec: `chatAskKey(request.id)`, `writeChatAsk(dir, request, now)`, `readChatAsks(dir)`, `writeChatAnswer(dir, key, answer)`, `readChatAnswer(dir, key)`, `writeChatSettled(dir, key, settled)`, `readChatSettled(dir, key)`, `writeChatNotice(dir, request, now)`, `takeChatNotices(dir)`, `writeChatHeartbeat(dir, now)`, `chatHeartbeatFresh(dir, nowMs)`, `removeChatHeartbeat(dir)`. Writers publish complete records only; `writeChatAsk` resolves to the key.

userStories.title: Guard child answers and fail safely
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Harden ChatAskPlugin against malformed answers, agent authority violations, cancellation and write failures.

**Motivation** — `initInteractionChain` returns null for headless + `cli` (`src/interaction/init.ts`), so a chat-launched run's tool approvals are denied `unavailable` and its triggers never reach a person.

**Approach** — Malformed answers (F3), the child-side agent guards (F7), `cancel`, an ask write failure with no fallback (F1) and an unknown request id. Tests in a new `test/unit/interaction/plugins/chat-guards.test.ts`.

F1: Child cannot write `<key>.ask.json` and has no fallback — `send` throws `NaxError` code `CHAT_ASK_WRITE_FAILED` (the existing callers already treat a thrown send as unavailable).
F3: `<key>.answer.json` is malformed JSON or has an unknown `action` — ignored with one warning; the child keeps waiting.
F7: A `chat-agent` answer names `allow-remember`, or answers a human-only ask — child downgrades `allow-remember` to `allow`; child ignores an agent answer to a human-only ask and keeps waiting.

Human-only means `request.metadata.safety === "red"` or `request.metadata.trigger` is `"pre-merge"` or `"human-review"`. Do not trust parent routing as the only authority check. For approvalPrompt asks downgrade the remembered approval value only for chat-agent; chat-user retains its choices. Cancellation returns a timeout response but records `by: "cancelled"`. Unknown ids reject with `CHAT_ASK_UNKNOWN`. Warnings use the constructor logger, default getSafeLogger().

**Scope** — In: plugin validation, defense-in-depth and guard tests. Out: fallback behavior (US-004), parent routing (US-012/013), changes to approval store/audit.

**Interface** — Preserve the existing `InteractionPlugin` contracts: `send(request: InteractionRequest): Promise<void>`, `receive(requestId: string, timeout?: number): Promise<InteractionResponse>`, `cancel?(requestId: string): Promise<void>`, `destroy?(): Promise<void>`. Use `_chatAskFileDeps` to drive write failures and `_chatAskPluginDeps` to advance time.

userStories.title: Initialize chat interaction chains and parse the hidden flag
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Allow an explicit ask directory to override headless CLI suppression and add the shared absolute-path flag parser.

**Motivation** — `initInteractionChain` returns null for headless + `cli` (`src/interaction/init.ts`), so a chat-launched run's tool approvals are denied `unavailable` and its triggers never reach a person.

**Approach** — A hidden `--chat-asks <dir>` flag (constant `CHAT_ASKS_FLAG`) names the job's ask directory. When it is present, `initInteractionChain` builds a chain whose single plugin is `ChatAskPlugin` (name `"chat"`), even in headless + `cli`. `ChatAskPlugin` wraps the plugin the project config names as its fallback when that plugin is not `cli` (Telegram or webhook); with `cli` there is no fallback. Every ask source already goes through the chain or its primary plugin, so nothing upstream changes. A flag, not an environment variable: an env var would be inherited by any nested `nax` the run's own agents start.

`ChatAskPlugin` has no `init` of its own. `InteractionChain.init` looks configs up by plugin name (`"chat"`), so `initInteractionChain` calls `fallback.init(config.interaction.config ?? {})` itself before constructing the plugin, and registers the chat plugin without calling `chain.init`.

Target: `initInteractionChain(config, headless, options?: { readonly chatAsksDir?: string })`; plugin construction goes through a new `_interactionInitDeps.createInteractionPlugin`. Forward `config.interaction.defaults.chatAskFallbackMs` as fallbackDelayMs. Without a directory, preserve existing behavior. Add `parseChatAsksFlag` in `src/cli/run-chat-asks.ts` (modelled on `src/cli/run-max-iterations.ts`). Undefined is absence; absolute paths pass through unchanged; relative paths return the exact message `--chat-asks must be an absolute path`.

**Scope** — In: init options/dependency seam, wrapped initialized fallback and pure parser, new `init-chat-asks.test.ts` and `run-chat-asks.test.ts`. Out: run flag threading (US-006), bot flag threading (US-007), config with no interaction section (preserve null).

**Interface** — `initInteractionChain(config, headless, options?: { readonly chatAsksDir?: string })`; parser results are `{ ok: true, value: undefined }`, `{ ok: true, value: absolutePath }` or `{ ok: false, message: "--chat-asks must be an absolute path" }`.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry the hidden run flag to real setup and expose an injectable interaction initializer.

**Motivation** — `initInteractionChain` returns null for headless + `cli` (`src/interaction/init.ts`), so a chat-launched run's tool approvals are denied `unavailable` and its triggers never reach a person.

**Approach** — `RunSetupOptions.chatAsksDir?: string`; calls `_runSetupDeps.initInteractionChain(config, headless, chatAsksDir ? { chatAsksDir } : undefined)`. `RunOptions` (`src/execution/runner.ts`), `RunnerSetupOptions` (`src/execution/runner-setup.ts`) and the run CLI options (`bin/run-action.ts`, `bin/run-action-execute.ts`, `bin/nax.ts`) carry `chatAsksDir` the same way they carry `headless`. The option is declared as `new Option("--chat-asks <dir>").hideHelp()`; the run action validates it with `parseChatAsksFlag` beside `parseMaxIterationsFlag` and on failure prints the message and exits 1, as that flag does.

The hidden option in `bin/nax.ts`, `RunCliOptions.chatAsks` and its validation in `bin/run-action.ts`, the hand-off in `bin/run-action-execute.ts`, `RunOptions.chatAsksDir` (`src/execution/runner.ts`), `RunnerSetupOptions.chatAsksDir` (`src/execution/runner-setup.ts`), and `RunSetupOptions.chatAsksDir` with `_runSetupDeps.initInteractionChain` (`src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts`). The CLI → `run()` hand-off is plain property passing like `headless` and is held by the type checker; the ACs pin the `setupRun` and `runSetupPhase` end. Tests in a new `test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-chat-asks.test.ts`.

F12: `--chat-asks` value is not an absolute path — `nax run` exits with "--chat-asks must be an absolute path". Pin the parse through US-005; review the process.exit branch without adding an executable run-action exit test.

userStories.title: Connect bot review and fix jobs to chat asks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the hidden bot flags and manage a chat interaction chain for review/fix step contexts.

**Motivation** — Bot review / fix pass no `interactionChain` to `buildPrStepContext`.

**Approach** — The hidden option on both bot commands, validation in `withBotInput` through `parseChatAsksFlag`, `chatAsksDir` on `BotReviewInput` / `BotFixInput` (passed through `runBotFixCycle` by its existing input spread), `initInteractionChain` added to `_botReviewDeps` (`src/bot/review-deps.ts`) and to `_botFixDeps`, building and destroying the chain in `reviewCheckout` and the fix step, and F8. Tests in a new `test/unit/bot/bot-chat-asks.test.ts` and new cases in `test/unit/cli/bot-review.test.ts`.

Bot deps. `_botReviewDeps` is defined in `src/bot/review-deps.ts` and re-exported by `review-run.ts`; `_botFixDeps` (`src/bot/fix-run.ts`) copies members of it by value at load. Target: `initInteractionChain` is a member of both `_botReviewDeps` and `_botFixDeps`, so a test stubs each one separately.

Bot inputs (`src/bot/review-run.ts`, `src/bot/fix-run.ts`, `src/cli/bot.ts`). Target: `chatAsksDir?: string` on both inputs; when set, the chain from `initInteractionChain(config, true, { chatAsksDir })` is passed as `interactionChain` and destroyed when the step ends.

F8: Bot job: `initInteractionChain` throws for the ask directory — warning; the bot step runs without a chain (today's behaviour).
F12: `--chat-asks` value is not an absolute path — `nax bot` prints it and exits 1.

Use `new Option("--chat-asks <dir>").hideHelp()` on both commands. Omit optional input/context keys when unset, not merely set to undefined. Cleanup must destroy the initialized chain once on completion/early exit/error while retaining existing context/log/runtime/checkout cleanup.

**Scope** — In: bot CLI parser/flags, input propagation, step-chain lifecycle and degradation warnings. Out: run CLI (US-006), bot cycle redesign, non-chat bot interaction behavior.

**Interface** — `chatAsksDir?: string` on `BotReviewInput` and `BotFixInput`; CLI raw option `chatAsks?: string`; chain initialization is `initInteractionChain(config, true, { chatAsksDir })` and is passed to `buildPrStepContext` as `interactionChain` only when available.

userStories.title: Prepare per-job ask directories before detached launch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give each ask-capable detached job its own directory/heartbeat and append the hidden flag.

**Motivation** — Slice 2 left this gap on purpose (`2026-10-27-nax-chat-workflow-dispatch-slice2-design.md` 4.6): the launch card warns "this run has no channel for its own asks; they will time out".

**Approach** — `DetachedJobs.launch` (`src/chat/jobs/job-runner.ts`). Target: for `run`, `bot_review`, `bot_fix` calls a new `_jobRunnerDeps.createAsksDir(dir, now)` (creates the directory and writes the first heartbeat, in one try block) and spawns `[...request.argv, CHAT_ASKS_FLAG, dir]`; the record stores the spawned argv. The existing `_jobRunnerDeps.mkdir` keeps serving `jobsDir` only.

All files live in one directory per job: `<outputDir>/chat-jobs/<jobId>.asks/` (helper `jobAsksDir(outputDir, jobId)` in `job-store.ts`).

F9: Job runner cannot create the ask directory or heartbeat — the job is spawned without `--chat-asks`; `job.note` says asks will not reach the chat.

`jobAsksDir` in `job-store.ts`; `_jobRunnerDeps.createAsksDir`; `DetachedJobs.launch` creates the directory and first heartbeat and appends the flag for `run`, `bot_review`, `bot_fix`; F9. Tests extend `test/unit/chat/jobs/job-runner.test.ts` and `test/unit/chat/jobs/job-store.test.ts`.

Update the existing start expectation from exactly request.argv to `[...request.argv, "--chat-asks", jobAsksDir(outputDir, job.id)]`; the spawn options assertion is unchanged. The clone test compares stored argv against the spawned argv; the invariant that mutating a returned record does not change the stored one is unchanged. Preserve caller argv and existing detached/log fd lifecycle.

**Scope** — In: path helper, createAsksDir seam, launch preparation, durable spawned argv, degradation note and existing tests. Out: adding ask support to plan jobs (their unchanged argv remains a regression assertion in this story); parsing run/bot flags (US-006/007), registry heartbeat refresh (US-010), directory pruning.

**Interface** — `jobAsksDir(outputDir, jobId)` returns `<outputDir>/chat-jobs/<jobId>.asks` (no trailing separator); `_jobRunnerDeps.createAsksDir(dir, now)` prepares both directory and first heartbeat before `_jobRunnerDeps.spawn`.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete agent routing, answer validation, escalation and streak accounting in the registry.

**Motivation** — Today the child's own asks (triggers, tool approvals, the agent's clarifying questions, precheck and paused-story prompts) never reach the chat.

**Approach** — The registry calls `routeRunAsk` for each new ask with `chainActive` from `chains.isActive(job.chainId)`: the agent notice queue (`peekNotice` / `takeNotice`), `answer`, `escalate`, the agent streak and `noteUserTurn`. Tests in a new `test/unit/chat/jobs/run-asks-agent.test.ts`.

**Who answers (user rulings 2026-10-29).** `routeRunAsk` returns `"human"` when any of: the job has no `chainId`; `chains.isActive(job.chainId)` is false (this also covers jobs re-attached after a chat restart, since chain state is session-local); `request.metadata.safety === "red"`; `request.metadata.trigger` is `"pre-merge"` or `"human-review"`; the agent has already been handed `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AGENT_ASKS` (3) asks since the last user turn. Otherwise `"agent"`. The order does not matter: every condition yields `"human"` and only their absence yields `"agent"`.

**Agent answers.** An agent-routed ask is queued as a notice (built by `buildRunAskNotice`) and delivered as a turn when the chat is idle, ahead of job and task notices. The agent answers with the no-card tool `nax-jobs__answer_ask` (`ask`, `answer`, `reason`) or answers `escalate`, which turns the ask into a human card. An agent answer applies once: `allow-remember` is refused for the agent. The answer shows as a transcript notice with the reason.

An ask the agent escalated still counts toward `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AGENT_ASKS`. If writing an agent answer fails, `answer` resolves `{ ok: false, message: "[chat] could not write the answer for <askId>" }`.

Queue `<jobId>/<key>` notices with buildRunAskNotice, not new prompt literals. Taking the notice removes only queued delivery, not agent-waiting state. A successful answer writes `respondedBy: "chat-agent"`, reason and per-type encoding; validates confirm/choose options and refuses allow-remember. Queue the exact note `[<jobId>] agent answered <answer>: <reason>`. Escalation removes the queued notice and raises the existing human card, not an answer file. Unknown/already-settled ids return the exact not-waiting error. External settlement removes stale notices and prevents answers. The fourth handed-off ask without a user turn goes to a human, and noteUserTurn resets that streak.

**Scope** — In: registry agent queue, routing call, authority checks, answer encoding/errors, escalation and streak. Out: pure builders (US-012), tool registration and idle TUI delivery (US-014), remembering approvals or restoring chain approval after restart.

**Interface** —

```ts
export interface RunAskReply { readonly answer: string; readonly reason: string }
export type RunAskResult = { readonly ok: true } | { readonly ok: false; readonly message: string };
```
